reading.body:
When traditional carriers decline AI risk, the market splits into ten mechanisms that self-insure, pool, exclude, or hedge it, from hyperscaler captives to catastrophe bonds for cloud outages.

The pattern is retreat and replacement. Standard carriers remove generative AI risk through exclusion endorsements and cap cover through reinsurance limits, pushing complex liability into surplus lines and Lloyds. In the space left open, hyperscalers form single parent captives, startups create mutual risk pools, and developers buy parametric micro-insurance on API and GPU availability. Catastrophe bonds hedge multi-day cloud shutdowns, while vendors back model performance commitments with underlying policies.

This matters for AI because compute availability and model output become insurable events rather than unmanaged operational risks. Certification-linked discounts tie coverage to third party safety audits, creating a financial incentive for verified reliability. The data lists mechanisms only; it does not show premium levels, capacity amounts, claims experience, or whether these instruments actually pay out when cloud outages or model failures occur. The only physical-infrastructure link present is automated claims processing for facilities, not grid or power risk.
